title: Root Edit approval requires a three-day Snapshot poll with 10% participation and 50% in favor
content:
A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 sets the vote: the Operational Facilitator "triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have 50% of votes in favor to be approved."

Read as a system rather than as three numbers, the choices lean consistently toward agility. Snapshot means the vote is off-chain signalling, not an on-chain execution; three days is short for a change to the Agent's founding document; and a 10% quorum with a simple majority means roughly 5% of circulating supply can carry an amendment.

That is only defensible because the vote is not the sole safeguard. The 1% proposal gate filters entry, the Facilitator's alignment finding filters content, and the Artifact Edit Restrictions bound what any outcome may contain. The low quorum is affordable because the electorate is not the last line of defence — it is the middle of three.

The residual risk is concentration: the same low quorum that prevents governance deadlock also means a small organized holder bloc can pass changes during a quiet three-day window, provided the Facilitator has already found them aligned.

Because Snapshot only signals, enactment remains a separate manual step (A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.5) performed by the Facilitator — the vote authorizes the edit, it does not perform it.
description: Off-chain voting with a low quorum and a short window buys amendment agility, at the cost of allowing a 5%-of-supply bloc to carry a change to the Agent's founding document.
